timeline.event: Construction on the bridge began during an era of large-scale projects to build the Twin Cities freeway system.
The bridge was completed and opened to traffic.
A median barrier, larger outside walls, and a thicker concrete deck were added to the bridge, causing additional loading.
Vehicles experienced black ice when the temperature reached −30 °F (−34 °C), leading to a major pile-up on the northbound side of the bridge.
The federal government gave the I-35W bridge a rating of structurally deficient, citing significant corrosion in its bearings.
MnDOT began inspecting the bridge annually.
The bridge was identified as the single most treacherous cold-weather spot in the Twin Cities freeway system due to a thin layer of black ice.
Additional median barrier, larger outside walls, and a thicker concrete deck modifications caused additional loading on the gusset plates.
Minnesota DOT began testing magnesium chloride solutions and a mixture with a corn-processing byproduct to reduce black ice.
The state embedded temperature-activated nozzles in the bridge deck to spray potassium acetate solution.
The automated de-icing spray system came into operation.
A study by the civil engineering department of the University of Minnesota addressed out-of-plane distortion and noted a concern about lack of redundancy in the main truss system.
An inspection produced photos that later revealed gusset-plate bowing.
The bridge was again rated as structurally deficient and received a sufficiency rating of 50 in the National Bridge Inventory database.
An inspection found problems of cracking and fatigue on the bridge.
A steel reinforcement project was planned for the bridge.
The steel reinforcement project was canceled in favor of periodic safety inspections after engineers realized drilling would weaken the bridge.
The central span and adjoining spans of the bridge suddenly collapsed into the river and onto the riverbanks during rush hour.
Governor Tim Pawlenty stated that the bridge had been scheduled to be replaced in 2020, and USDOT granted Minnesota $5 million.
About 1,400 people gathered for an interfaith service of healing at St. Mark's Episcopal Cathedral.
President Bush signed into law $250 million in emergency funding passed unanimously by Congress.
The Hennepin County Board of Commissioners voted to request a major disaster area declaration, and Minnesotans held a minute of silence during National Night Out.
The American Red Cross lowered flags in remembrance, having counseled 2,000 people and served 7,000 meals.
Peters announced an additional $5 million for transit operations and $50 million in immediate emergency relief.
Mayor Rybak remembered each of the victims and the details of their lives during an address to the city council.
Governor Pawlenty requested a major disaster designation and made a request to the SBA.
Governor Pawlenty held a press conference and briefing with President Bush, estimating total emergency response costs over $8 million.
Small businesses harmed by the bridge collapse became eligible to apply for SBA loans.
MnDOT announced that Flatiron Construction and Manson Construction Co. would build the replacement bridge for $234 million.
The demolition operation was substantially complete.
Construction began on the new I-35W bridge.
The NTSB announced its interim determination that the bridge's design specified undersized and inadequate steel gusset plates.
The NTSB announced an investigative update noting that June 2003 photos showed gusset-plate bowing.
The state of Minnesota reached a $38 million agreement to compensate victims of the bridge collapse.
The orchestral piece 'The Bridge' composed by Osmo Vänskä premiered.
The replacement I-35W Saint Anthony Falls Bridge opened to the public at 5 a.m.
The NTSB released its final investigation findings, identifying 0.5-inch undersized gusset plates as the primary cause.
The last lawsuits against URS Corporation were settled for $52.4 million.
Debris temporarily stored at Bohemian Flats was removed to a storage facility in Afton, Minnesota.

legacy.what: The Federal Highway Administration advised states to inspect 700 U.S. bridges of similar construction after the gusset plate flaw was discovered.
The replacement I-35W Saint Anthony Falls Bridge was completed and opened to the public.
